BAO.basis: Wolof cereal/cattle economy, weaving and metalcraft, royal commercial diplomacy; Becker/Martin 1975.

SLU.basis: Cereal/cattle economy, dyeing/weaving and salt/river trade; Guelwar monarchy and commercial treaties. Culture identifiers are inherited regional proxies, not Serer ethnography.

TMB.basis: Resident Arma/civic authority, Niger-Saharan trade, salt extraction and merchant credit/accounting, craft economy and military garrison. Parentless era-1 salt/merchant capabilities support inherited salt mine and ordinary exchange PM; no maritime insurance or modern central bank granted.

TDM.basis: Pastoral Tuareg confederation, dependent Niger-bank cultivators, caravan diplomacy and armed retainers. Country knowledge includes subject cultivators, not only the ruling pastoral elite; specialised textile organisation is not separately certified.

GAO.basis: Existing Tag reactivated for local Arma and riverine communities, not the Songhay imperial footprint. Garrison, craft and Niger trade capabilities.

SNU.basis: Plural Senufo agricultural/ironworking/weaving communities; no Kenedugu/Sikasso kingdom projected back from nineteenth century.

KNN.basis: Kano walled towns, military establishments, organised weaving/dyeing and long-distance trade; UNESCO V chapter 16.

KTS.basis: Katsina merchant and textile centre with walled royal administration and garrison; UNESCO V chapter 16.

DAU.basis: Small established Hausa monarchy, agriculture/cattle, artisans, diplomacy and royal retainers. Specialised textile organisation not separately certified.

KEB.basis: Kebbi river agriculture, pastoral economy, craft trade and military monarchy; Lovejoy map and UNESCO V. No caliphal administration inferred.

ZAM.basis: Zamfara surviving royal districts, agricultural and military organisation, independent of the future caliphate; eighteenth-century map and account.

ZAZ.basis: Zazzau royal towns and tributary agricultural districts, cavalry/retainers and regional diplomacy; Lovejoy map.

NUP.basis: Nupe monarchy, Niger trade, craft/weaving and military establishments. Native hausa/tiv IDs are broad compatibility proxies; no Nupe culture exists in the installed catalogue.

ZRM.basis: Plural western Niger/Zarma communities, not a new united kingdom of Dosso; rural production and retained native military-site capacity.

GWR.basis: Plural Gbagyi/Gwari communities outside Zazzau core, not a centralised invented state. Broad native culture proxies retained as a model limitation.

BCH.basis: Plural plateau and Benue communities before the nineteenth-century emirate; inherited traditional military-site capacity, no united Bauchi emirate.

BTA.basis: Plural Bata, Mbum, Chamba and neighbouring communities; geographic decentralised aggregate, not an Adamawa emirate or single ethnic state. Native culture proxies are imprecise.

MDR.basis: Dulo/Doulo sultanate, royal retainers, farming/cattle, iron/textiles and exchange with Bornu; Barkindo UNESCO V ch17. Kanuri is a native regional proxy, not a Mandara ethnic census.

BIL.basis: Bilala/Yao authority around Lake Fitri; cereal cultivation, livestock, fishing and market exchange. Baguirmi is a broad native linguistic-area proxy; exact 1776 external tribute is unresolved.

DLS.basis: Daju frontier sultanate, cattle/farming, metalworking, armed retainers and negotiation with Wadai/Darfur; Kapteijns 1983 and Triaud 1990. Fur is a native regional proxy; no Daju culture exists.

SNR.basis: Funj/Hamaj court on Blue Nile, irrigated/rain-fed farming, livestock, weaving, craft production, caravan diplomacy and established military service; Hasan/Ogot ch7.

ABD.basis: Northern Funj feudatories, Nile/Atbara and Butana chiefly communities, farming/livestock, weaving, crafts, trade and armed retainers; Hasan/Ogot and O Fahey/Spaulding. Aggregate political envelope, not direct administration of every village.

SHQ.basis: Independent Nile-bend chiefly kingdoms with cavalry/retainers, river agriculture, cattle, weaving and trading contacts. The country aggregates several makks; not a single invented dynasty.

DNG.basis: Zubayr makks before the Shayqiyya conquest of the 1780s; river farming, cattle, weaving, crafts and Nile commerce. Sudanese is the available Nubian-area proxy; nuba is deliberately not substituted for Nubian.

NUB.basis: Hereditary Nubian kashifs and fortified garrison corridor south of Aswan, nominal Ottoman-Egyptian dependency; Hasan/Ogot and Beska. Distinct from Dongola and from the Egyptian conquest of 1820/21.

MSB.basis: Hashim/Musabbaat central Kordofan royal and military network, farming/cattle, craft and caravan contacts, restored around 1772; O Fahey/Spaulding 1972. Not Darfur annexation of 1785/86.

TQL.basis: Northeastern Nuba highland kings and protective brokerage, cereal/cattle economy, iron crafts and armed service. Ewald 1990/published archaeological reconnaissance; exact consolidation date and alleged Funj tributary relation remain debated.

SLQ.basis: Reth kingship, sedentary cattle/cereal villages and Nile ferry/trade authority up to Alays attested by Bruce in 1772; Hasan/Ogot ch7. Nilotic is the native broad culture identifier, not a Dinka replacement.

SRA.basis: Native dormant Sara tag activated for plural southern Chari communities; raiding/tribute spheres are not permanent Wadai government. Rural capabilities only, no united Sara kingdom asserted.

TGR.basis: Tigrayan provincial lordship, highland agriculture, textiles/craft and armed retainers. University Hist.102 p107; northern regional core compared with Bahru p17 and Haberland. Not a modern ethnic-region boundary.

GJM.basis: Gojjam lordship within the Blue Nile loop, provincial grain/cattle economy, craft and military retinue. Hist.102 pp107,117; regional approximation from river/locality comparison.

WLO.basis: Wollo and adjoining Lasta chiefly networks; cereal/pastoral economy, craft, negotiation and retainers. Aggregate autonomy, not the later Yejju hegemony founded in 1786.

SHW.basis: Ankober/Menz/Yifat Shewan dynastic core under Asfa Wosen from 1775; Hist.102 p92. Excludes nineteenth-century expansion and the future Addis Ababa metropolis.

KFA.basis: Independent Kaffa court in the southwest, agricultural/textile/craft and exchange capability; Haberland pp802-805. Bonga core only, not modern Kaffa administrative province.

WLT.basis: Wolayta kingship attested before the eighteenth century, agrarian production and royal retainers; Haberland pp804-805. Oral dynastic legends do not certify each frontier.

AWS.basis: Awsa lower-Awash oasis polity, Afar court, agriculture/pastoralism, exchange and armed retainers; Haberland p789 and Hist.102. Not direct sovereignty over every Afar coastal sultanate.

HAR.basis: Independent Harar emirate and surrounding local authority, agriculture/crafts/textiles, caravan exchange and armed service; Hist.102 p92. Native Amhara culture is a catalogue proxy, not an ethnic claim.

YJR.basis: Janjero/Yem court between Gibe and Omo systems, established before 1776; Haberland p805. Two-province core and native Sidama proxy, not full modern district or dynastic reconstruction.

HRI.basis: Hiraab imamate/confederate authority and Mogadishu/central coast after Ajuran fragmentation; Kluijver thesis ch2 and Cassanelli ch4. Confederation, not homogeneous central administration.

WLG.basis: Wallaga/Macha Oromo communities under Gadaa and local authorities before the nineteenth-century Leqa monarchies. Hist.102 pp114-116 and Mohammed Hassen SOAS thesis.

ARS.basis: Arsi and adjacent Oromo Gadaa communities east of the Rift; not a nineteenth-century monarchical state. Haberland regional narrative and Hist.102.

BRN.basis: Borana pastoral and Gadaa communities in the south, outside Gondarine direct government. Native tag, not a unitary sultanate.

OMO.basis: Plural southern/Omo communities outside reviewed royal cores. Native aggregate does not claim a single monarchy or ethnic homogeneity; Haberland pp802-805.

BJA.basis: Beja/Bilen/Habab western lowlands, local authorities distinct from Asmara highlands and Ottoman harbours. Aggregate native tag; not a unified Beja kingdom.

OGD.basis: Interior Somali pastoral communities outside Ethiopian direct authority; not a modern national boundary or ethnically uniform cadastral partition.

AFR.basis: Plural Afar coastal and desert authorities outside Awsa royal core; maritime contacts and the inherited coastal anchorage. Ottoman claims do not establish direct highland administration.

HDY.basis: Autonomous Hadiya/Kambata highland communities, Hist.102 pp113-114; a plural local envelope, not revival of the vast medieval Hadiya kingdom.

LNG.basis: Vansina pp636-637: Loango crown and council still exist in 1776; succession collapse after1787 is not projected backwards. Coastal agriculture, raffia weaving, craft and commerce; no automatic pastoral or military grant. Dependency clarification: Proyart1776, chapterVI,p32(PDF38), records pigs/goats/sheep and fowl in the coastal kingdoms; small-stock capability closes the agricultural parent. For Tio interior this is a documented regional inference, not attestation of a large cattle sector.

TKE.basis: Vansina pp604,636: Tio/Makoko kingdom, autonomous magnates and river commerce; civil war fromc1780 is later. Craft gate is capability, not assertion of local iron smelting; no textile/pastoral blanket grant. Dependency clarification: Proyart1776, chapterVI,p32(PDF38), records pigs/goats/sheep and fowl in the coastal kingdoms; small-stock capability closes the agricultural parent. For Tio interior this is a documented regional inference, not attestation of a large cattle sector.

YKA.basis: Vansina p642: Kwango Yaka kingdom formed1740-1760, conquering eastward before1776; royal and military organisation, agricultural and textile/craft exchange. Native territorial envelope remains approximate.

KSN.basis: Vansina pp618-621,642: Kasanje kingdom and Imbangala armed caravans on the upperKwango, distinct from Matamba and Portuguese Kwanza posts; mixed cultivation/husbandry/craft and commerce.

SYO.basis: Vansina pp620-621 and Thornton chapter discussed in scholarly synthesis: autonomous Soyo survived the Kongo collapse; Mpinda/Soyo south of river. Agriculture, weaving/craft, maritime exchange and organised royal forces; no claim of modern Portuguese protection.

KKG.basis: Vansina pp634-636: Kakongo court and Malemba trade after1750. Independent coastal polity north of Ngoyo, regional agri/textile/craft exchange; no claim to a livestock sector. Dependency clarification: Proyart1776, chapterVI,p32(PDF38), records pigs/goats/sheep and fowl in the coastal kingdoms; small-stock capability closes the agricultural parent. For Tio interior this is a documented regional inference, not attestation of a large cattle sector.

NGY.basis: Vansina pp635-636: Ngoyo court and Cabinda port before Portuguese incursion1783. Small north-bank estuary polity, agriculture, raffia craft and commerce; no1783 occupation in1776. Dependency clarification: Proyart1776, chapterVI,p32(PDF38), records pigs/goats/sheep and fowl in the coastal kingdoms; small-stock capability closes the agricultural parent. For Tio interior this is a documented regional inference, not attestation of a large cattle sector.

MTM.basis: Vansina pp614-620,641-642: Matamba court separate from Kasanje, upper interior east of Kwanza presidios; native Ovimbundu is catalogue proxy for Mbundu, not ethnic correction. Royal Christianity coexisted with local cults; agriculture, craft and armed service.

MBL.basis: Vansina p642: Mbailundu and Bihe royal development accelerated by campaigns from1772; highland cultivation, cattle, textiles, crafts, armed retinues and caravan exchanges. Small Bailundo nucleus north of Huambo, not all later kingdom.

BIE.basis: Vansina pp641-642: Bihé kingdom sheltering quimbares after1772; Cuito/Bié plateau east of Bailundo, agrarian/pastoral/textile/craft exchanges and royal armed service, no nineteenth-century expansion envelope.

DMB.basis: Vansina pp604,635 and Africana Studia25p42: independent connected Ndembu authorities around Encoje, not direct Kongo or Portuguese administration. Mixed indigenous cultivation/craft, native culture proxies; no single sovereign Dembo monarchy.

KIS.basis: Vansina regional map641 and Kwanza occupation history: plural independent local authorities south of Kwanza outside Portuguese posts and Ovimbundu royal nuclei. Native regional rural/craft profile, not a unitary Kisama state or complete ethnic partition.

MYU.basis: Vansina p636: distant Mayumba provinces seceded from Loango from1750. Southern Gabon coastal/local chiefdom aggregate only; inherited native Bakongo proxy, agriculture/raffia/craft, no unified new Mayumba monarchy. Dependency clarification: Proyart1776, chapterVI,p32(PDF38), records pigs/goats/sheep and fowl in the coastal kingdoms; small-stock capability closes the agricultural parent. For Tio interior this is a documented regional inference, not attestation of a large cattle sector.

KSC.fr: Pays du Kasaï et du Sankuru
KSC.adj_fr: pays du kasaï et du sankuru
KSC.basis: Outside the retained Bushong/Kuba royal core: plural local communities between Kasai/Sankuru/Lulua. UNESCO20pp643-651; native culture cohorts preserved, no unitary new monarchy.

LKS.basis: UNESCO20p649,651: Luba migrations north into Kasai, not direct extension of the Upemba royal administration. Existing native ethnic portion retained as local communities, no forced tributary link.

MIA.basis: UNESCO20map20.3 and expansion chronologypp648-656: forest and northern communities outside the reviewed eighteenth-century Upemba core; not wholesale nineteenth-century royal expansion.

LMP.basis: UNESCO20pp643-660: southeastern copper communities outside the Luapula court. Locally attested preindustrial copper shafts justify shaft_mining for inherited mine rights/PM; no engines or industrial tier granted.

ZPL.basis: Plural Ila/Tonga/Nkoya/Lala and adjoining plateau communities outside the early Luyana floodplain nucleus. Mainga SOAS thesis abstract and Hogan chapter5 distinguish valley nucleus from later expansion. Broad residual envelope is explicit, not a tribal cadastral claim.

LVL.basis: UNESCO20pp655,660-661: upper-Zambezi western communities and Lwena/Lunda contacts. Native river/locality envelope only; no single Luvale monarchy or automatic subject status.

MLG.basis: North Zambia/Tanganyika local communities outside the small early Bemba nucleus; Roberts1970chronology abstract and UNESCO21regional framework. Not nineteenth-century Bemba conquests.

BSI.basis: UNESCO21pp691-692: Bisa routes and reputation explicitly attested by1775; autonomous ivory carriers outside direct Bemba or Kazembe annexation. No unified royal kingdom asserted.

TBK.basis: UNESCO21regional chronology and metallurgypp692-693: northern Malawi Tumbuka communities. No attempt to date every Chikulamayembe succession or unify all local chiefdoms.

NGD.basis: UNESCO21pp684-685: Kyungu royal power at Karonga plain before1720 and consolidation under Kasyombe c1750. Two native northern-Malawi cells, no expansion under Mwangonde after1785. Mixed farming/craft, exchange and royal retainers.

KNY.basis: UNESCO20p649,656: Kanyok royal authority under Luba overlordship before the crisis1780-1810. MweneDitu/Kanyok native nucleus; tributary status models autonomy without exact fiscal schedule.

BUS.basis: UNESCO26pp855,862: nine states existed by1750, remaining distinct from Buganda. Plural autonomous royal/chiefly aggregate, not the later single Kyabazinga institution. Agriculture, stock, craft/weaving and lake exchanges.

GSK.basis: UNESCO26pp876-889: independent Gisaka east of Rwanda and linked to Karagwe; native single-cell royal envelope, not nineteenth-century Rwandan annexation. The disconnected northern candidate was excluded before installation.

BGE.basis: UNESCO26pp886-890: Bugesera still a political neighbour; partition at opening of nineteenth century. One native southern-Rwanda cell approximates royal core, no ruler chronology claimed.

BHA.basis: UNESCO26p887: northern Buha Bahumbi court before decline in mid19c. Native Malagarazi/Buyungu envelope, not direct Nyamwezi government.

BHS.basis: UNESCO26p887: Ruguru/Heru/Bushingo southern royal line separate from northern Buha. Western Tanganyika/Malagarazi native-cell envelope; no later Vinza chiefdom founded1800.

KIZ.basis: UNESCO26pp887-888: Kiziba between Kagera and Victoria, royal polity independent of later Buganda interventions; local agrarian/pastoral/artisanal exchange.

KYM.basis: UNESCO26pp887-888: neighbouring royal powers on westVictoria coast, represented together at available two-cell scale. Not annexation by Karagwe or later Maruku/Bugabo fragmentations.

UDI.basis: UNESCO21pp678-687: Undi Chewa monarchy west/southwest of Kalonga, weakened but not abolished by eighteenth-century fragmentation. No Ngoni/Maseko state before migrations.

LDU.basis: UNESCO21pp677-687: Lundu lowerShire monarchy with reduced influence; no direct sovereignty over all Makua and Lomwe interior in1776.

UTV.basis: UNESCO22pp714-719 and coastal trading context: Uteve hinterland of Sofala, independent African authority distinct from Portuguese coastal fort. No Tswana realm placed here.

TCH.basis: Mozambique southern coastal communities; HPIP Inhambane and Hedges Delagoa Bay thesis distinguish local authorities from forts. No nineteenth-century Gaza/Ngoni/Tswana monarchy; existing POP attributes preserved, cultural reconstruction remains open. Native tonga is a broad Southern Bantu country-culture proxy, not a claim of ethnic identity; tsonga is not a valid engine culture.

TMP.basis: Mathebula2017 NewContree78pp42-57 abstract: Tembe royal power at its late18c apogee south of MaputoBay. Small native-bay envelope; local Mpfumo/Maputo subdivisions unresolved. Hedges and peer-reviewed2024 study distinguish commerce from a permanent Portuguese territorial post. Native tonga is a broad Southern Bantu country-culture proxy; no POP conversion or new culture.

LND.basis: UNESCO20pp655-660: central Rund/MwataYamvo realm around Mussumba; loose tributary empire, not a uniform colonial province.

LBA.basis: UNESCO20pp648-656: eighteenth-century Upemba/Lualaba royal core, northern/eastern19c expansion excluded.

KZM.basis: UNESCO20pp659-660: Luapula/Mweru Kazembe court founded before1776, nominal imperial tribute with broad internal autonomy.

KBA.basis: UNESCO20pp643-651 and Bushong/Kuba region: retain compact royal core, distinguish adjoining communities. Independent pre-existing state, not a detached province of a distant parent.

LZO.basis: Mainga1968 SOAS abstract; Hogan2015ch5: Luyana kingship fromc17c, floodplain nucleus distinct from later expansive Lozi/Barotse sphere. Kingship historically attested; inherited decentralised engine classification retained for this territorial lot, so no central enclave or fictional corridor to Portugal is created. Institutional refinement remains open.

BMB.basis: Roberts1970 chronology: early Chitimukulu court probably17c; no precise ruler chronology or late18c/19c expansion imposed.
BMB.targeted_grant_basis: Roberts1970 Chitimukulu regional political contacts; UNESCO21 regional exchange before later expansion. Minimal early diplomatic/market capability for private trade customs, not commercial insurance or a modern foreign ministry.

MRV.basis: UNESCO21pp678-687: Kalonga royal nucleus under eighteenth-century fragmentation, not all Maravi peoples or whole northernMozambique.

MTP.basis: UNESCO22 Mutapa court survives, reduced after Portuguese penetration and Rozvi secession; no whole empire of the16c reinstalled.

MNC.basis: UNESCO22pp714-741: Manica/Manyika royal and trading authority, not unstructured empty land; Rozvi overlordship chronology left for southern phase.
MNC.targeted_grant_basis: UNESCO22pp714-719: Manyika court negotiations and commerce with Portuguese traders and neighbouring powers. Minimal early diplomatic/market capability for private trade customs, not commercial insurance or a modern foreign ministry.

MKU.basis: Makua/Makonde local chiefdoms after Maravi decline; Alpers2021JAMH5p8 records independence and trade disputes around MozambiqueIsland.

LMW.basis: UNESCO21pp677-687: Lomwe/Lolo authorities rejecting Lundu suzerainty during eighteenth century, farming and iron/craft.

UYA.basis: UNESCO21pp689-692: Yao homeland east ofMalawi and ivory caravans to coast before1776, not later militarised slave states.

SNA.basis: Sena/Shire-Zambezi local communities outside Crown posts and prazos; no single central monarchy claimed.

CHW.basis: UNESCO21pp678-687: Chewa local authorities outside reviewed Kalonga/Undi/Lundu courts; native plural aggregate, not empty land.

AVR.basis: Kent28pp949-951; Berg1988 extract: northern Imerina royal court distinct from Antananarivo before consolidation. Two native cells approximate the northern royal sector; court coordinates overlap the scale of neighbouring native cells, no precise cadastral boundary claimed. Irrigated rice, cattle, textile/metal craft, exchanges and royal armed retainers.

AHI.basis: Kent28p950-951: western Imerina royal power not conquered until later1790s. Native western royal-sector envelope, not a new pixel-level palace boundary. Rice/cattle, weaving/workshops and court/market relations.

BOI.basis: Kent28pp943-947: northwestern Sakalava court, markets and tribute networks, distinct from Menabe and Merina. Royal nucleus and adjoining directly associated western hinterland; not wholesale annexation of every tributary. Trading and military organisation; no commercial-insurance or gun-manufacturing technology.

MEB.basis: Kent28pp940-945: separate western Sakalava monarchy, riverine royal framework and stock/market economy; northern Boina distinct. Native coastal/interior envelope between western interfaces, not all ethnic Sakalava treated as direct subjects.

ATK.basis: Kent28pp945-947: northern royal line and organisation borrowed from Boina, tribute attested before1776; autonomy preserved with native tributary pact. No claimed accession date installed. Native offshore islands remain with their mainland provinces.

TMH.basis: Kent28pp945-946: autonomous upper-Sofia/Mandritsara communities, no central kingdom or regular tribute. Rural farming/cattle/craft capabilities, no fictional monarch.

BSM.basis: Kent28pp955-957,944: local filohany and autonomous clans persist after confederation; coastal armed commerce, royal influence and disputed Boina tribute do not equal uniform administration. Plural engine aggregate, not a single new national monarchy. Benyowsky/French coastal installations remain a documented local limitation.

SNK.basis: Kent28pp951-952: fortified Alaotra communities, potters, bridge and trade; no central authority. Historical Boina tribute not converted into direct provincial rule or a native centralised-subject pact.

BZN.basis: Kent28pp951-952: Ankay forest-route communities and fortified villages under local mpifehy; later short-lived kingship not projected automatically into1776. Indigenous markets/textile/metal craft and regional exchange.

ANR.basis: Kent28p951: western Imamo and Betafo/Andratsay powers submitted only during later Merina consolidation. Explicit plural aggregate of distinct local authorities, potentially separated by royal cores; no unified ethnic monarchy claimed.

ISD.basis: Kent28pp947-949: eighteenth-century Andriamanalina court, royal rice/cattle reforms and diplomacy/armed retainers. Extent of hegemony and its chronology not treated as direct possession of all Betsileo.

LLG.basis: Kent28pp947-948: independent Betsileo court, national militia and rice reforms, resistance to later Merina demands. Court retained separately from Isandra, no exact1776 ruler invented.

MDN.basis: Kent28pp947-949: royal formation afterc1750, submission to Merina c1800. Northern Betsileo three-cell court envelope, no forced1776 subject status.

RND.basis: Kent28pp947-948: southern Betsileo royal formation distinct from Lalangina/Isandra, neighbouring Bara. Native southern highland envelope; internal/later Isandra hegemony not certified as permanent direct rule.

ATM.basis: Kent28pp923-926,953,958: Matitana coastal royal society, sorabe specialists, rice/overseas commerce and royal conflict with Ikongo. National culture malagasy is a native proxy; no POP religion conversion or blanket Islamic state imposed.

BHK.basis: Kent28pp955,958: distinct southeastern coastal royal formation outside Betsimisaraka/Merina, around Mananjary. Small native littoral envelope, detailed dynasty/chronology unresolved.

ATF.basis: Kent28pp957-958: Ambaky/Farafangana royal power and maritime trade, distinct from Antemoro and Antesaka. Two native coastal-interface cells, no exact succession date asserted.

ASK.basis: Kent28pp957-958: Nosipandra/Vangaindrano royal line and rice economy; independent political formation before later Merina expansion. Native coastal sector, not precise final boundaries under late18c rulers.

MSR.basis: Kent28p932 and regional southwest discussion: Andrevola royal power in Fiherenana valley distinct from Sakalava-Maroserana. Coastal valley/river envelope, not uniform control over all southern Masikoro communities.

IKO.basis: Kent28pp952-953: Zafirambo royal centre recorded since1668, local law/ritual specialists and fortified royal rock, conflicts with Antemoro. Rice/cattle/craft and royal guard model; no later Merina alliance at start.

TNL.basis: Kent28pp952-953: plural forest communities outside distinct Ikongo royal centre, never one all-Tanala state. Native northern forest sector, rural/craft capabilities without national institutions.

BAR.basis: Kent28pp953-955: multiple Zafimanely/clan kings and strong local councils, no single sovereign over all Ibara. Plural political aggregate, not absence of chiefs; pastoral/rural craft, no post1800 consolidation.

MHF.basis: Kent28pp939-941: four independent Mahafaly kingdoms and clan authorities, not a single national monarchy. Native southwest strip aggregated at available scale; internal royal authority acknowledged, unresolved internal borders not invented.

ATY.basis: Kent28pp958-959: many small local kings in Ambolo/Mandrare, no unified large Antanosy state. Native southeast envelope; FortDauphin settlement attempt1767-1770 not projected as continuous French territorial administration.

TDY.basis: Kent28pp959-960: Karimbola autonomy and weakening Zafimanara confederation, continued local leaders, no whole southern peninsula ruled from Imerina. Pastoral/craft capabilities, no specific collapse date forced.

CMO.basis: Kent28pp960-964: separate island sultanates and rival local courts, no Merina authority. One inherited native province covers the archipelago; explicit plural autonomous aggregate rather than a unified Comorian state. Ports/craft/commerce model, not a historical national constitution.

MAD.basis: Existing MAD retained as Antananarivo royal core; no island-wide Merina dominion in1776. Original technologies retained, no automatic industrial or military grant. Ruler/precise court boundary not invented.

NST.basis: Denoon23pp750-754; Hamilton/Wright2026 sections moving political mosaic and dynamic sovereignty; Bonner1983pp9-13. Northern Nguni farming and chiefly communities between Drakensberg and ocean; no unified Shaka empire in1776 and no Tswana sovereignty over Natal. Plural native coastal envelope; individual Mthethwa/Ndwandwe/Hlubi borders not invented.

HVD.basis: Denoon23map23.1,pp750-754; Hamilton/Wright2026 mobility and political mosaics, archaeological references to Highveld stone settlements. Local Sotho/Tswana/Nguni authorities replace Transvaal republic and broad later Matabele envelope. Not a single Highveld state or cadastral tribal map; agriculture, cattle, local metal and textile crafts/exchanges. Organised chiefly/Orange-frontier armed followings (Denoon23pp750-754,761-762) justify the early military-establishments gate of inherited barracks; no industrial arms-production grant.

KQO.basis: Denoon23pp749,761 and map23.1; University Free State Griquatown heritage entry: San/Korana before mission1800-1804, Griqua state/name1813, Waterboer later. Plural Kora/San and neighbouring communities of middle Orange-Vaal; no Philippolis or Waterboer state in1776. Khoisan/Tswana national proxies only, inherited Griqua/Boer POP identities not converted. Organised chiefly/Orange-frontier armed followings (Denoon23pp750-754,761-762) justify the early military-establishments gate of inherited barracks; no industrial arms-production grant.

MSH.basis: Bhila22pp714-718,map22.8 after Beach1984p38: Changamire royal formation centred on Butwa/Danangombe/Khami with extensive tributary authority; Manyika subordinate, Mutapa distinct. Retained native60-cell envelope is broad and includes uncertain western/northern margins. Court/army/craft/markets justify only early diplomatic and military capabilities, not industrial grants.

BST.basis: Denoon23map23.1,pp750-754; no unified Moshoeshoe Basotho kingdom in1776. Plural Sotho authorities on Caledon/Drakensberg and adjacent Highveld. Existing knowledge and formations retained; later national polity/journal not projected backwards.

MTB.basis: SAHO, The Ndebele in history, Early History (2011/update2026), section actually retrieved; Denoon23 regional geography/craft. Distinguish older southern-Ndebele Manala/Ndzundza authorities from Mzilikazi nineteenth-century polity. Seven native Pretoria/Wonderboom cells are a limited regional approximation, not a complete surveyed boundary. HIA2023 remains an indexed lead only. Capital corrected to TRANSVAAL; national Shona removed, POPs unchanged.

SWZ.basis: Bonner1983pp9-13: Ngwane in Shiselweni1760s-1770s; later expansion north not dated1776. Retain existing three-cell political nucleus and NgwaneIII rather than erase autonomy. Native northern extent is unresolved, explicitly not certified as cadastral or modern Swazi border.

TSH.basis: Pospelov1800 introduction: four separately governed dahas before Yunus1784; aggregate urban polity, not an already unified khanate. Irrigated oasis, weaving, workshops and caravan diplomacy; early capabilities only.

URT.basis: Beisembiev/Levi, initial18c stage and Bregel: autonomous Yuz domains around Ura-Tepa/Khujand, intermittently contested. Native western Fergana envelope; irrigated cultivation and urban crafts, no19c army or banking grant.

QTG.basis: Bregel: mountain principality before Kokand1830s expansion; Garm/Rasht valley native approximation. Small-stock cultivation, textiles, local crafts and external negotiation, no industrial knowledge inferred.

KLB.basis: Bregel lists Kolab among mountain principalities independent of the later Kokand/Bukharan annexations. Two native cells east of inherited Bukharan Hissar portion, west of Darvaz; northern nucleus only, no southern-bank transfer. Lowland cultivation, craft and local external negotiation.

SHG.basis: Grevemeyer, Darvaz: eastern semiautonomous Shughnan/Rushan, generally tied to Badakhshan. Two courts aggregated in northern native cells; precise1776 allegiance not proved, no invented DUR pact. Native Tajik/Shiite catalogue proxies for Pamiri/Ismaili populations; no POP assimilation.

KYR.basis: Saparaliyev2011 pp142,144,148,155 cites18c independent Kyrgyz authorities and Osh-Alay/highland communities. Decentralized aggregate, not modern Kyrgyzstan or a unified kingdom; pastoral cultivation and household crafts, no blanket diplomacy/military tier.
